dedupe_keys.name: iea wind task 43 wra data model json schema for wind resource measurement stations and calibration certificates

description: The WRA Data Model is an open standard for describing how a wind or solar resource measurement station is built and configured, so that measurement campaigns can be exchanged and processed automatically in energy yield assessments. It is produced by IEA Wind Task 43 with industry and research members, and the repository also holds a digital calibration certificate schema and a floating lidar file format. Coverage: generic, used internationally for met masts, lidar, sodar, floating lidar and solar stations. A data model instance records the station location, mast geometry, each sensor with serial number, mounting height and boom orientation, logger programming such as slopes and offsets, calibrations and how all of these changed over time. Format and access: JSON Schema files with demo data, documentation, a form-based app and conversion tools on GitHub; release V1.4.0-2025.06 is the latest; free. Licence: BSD-3-Clause style (copyright Alliance for Sustainable Energy, NREL). Caveats: it is a schema, not measurement data, and adoption by logger vendors and consultancies is still partial. Simulation uses: a consistent metadata layer for wind resource measurements used in capacity planning of wind farms and in turbine digital twin validation. Related records: the Kelmarsh wind farm SCADA data (data-kelmarsh-wind-farm-scada) and the wtDigiTwin model (model-wtdigitwin-wind-turbine-digital-twin) are measurement and twin resources that such metadata supports.
